chronology: [Recap] Othon cannot father children; Honorata conceives Aghnar using a drop of his blood. Two jealous servants push her from the fortress during pregnancy; Othon fires an epyphite cartridge so she floats to safety, but Aghnar is born lighter than air. Honorata fits him with steel bracelets and exiles herself with him to the sacred mountain of Ansirma to train his mind and pain tolerance.

[Recap, age 7] Aghnar returns to the Castaka fortress for Othon's warrior test. He defeats a robot and endures a machine that crushes his feet without yielding; he receives metal prosthetic feet. This event canonizes ritual mutilation and prosthetic replacement as the Metabaron initiation rite.

[Current story opens] Robot servant awaits master Lothar in a futuristic industrial complex. The Metabaron arrives violently, breaching the structure. Observers detect an energy beam cutting the Metabunker in half; emergency reactor activation (B-570-4890) is required to reunite its two halves before they fall into an acid lake. Ant-robots make repairs.

[Narrative frame] Tonto recounts the Metabarons saga to Lothar. Robots debate the current Metabaron's invincibility; a chronomatrix is used to date a scar on his right eyebrow. The storyteller defers the scar explanation and pivots to the episode of the whore-priestesses.

[Approaching Okhar] Mother Superior's Shabda-Oud vessel approaches Okhar from space with hidden weapons. Her alpha-plus intuition senses an anomaly; she orders extreme caution. Separately, three whore-priestesses board a Harana-class robo-transporter whose catayborg controller has been sedated with pentalina for two hours.

[Delegation arrives] The Shabda-Oud delegation reaches the Castaka fortress. In a psychically swept, soundproof chamber they interrogate Honorata: seven years ago she was ordered to produce and surrender a hermaphrodite child destined to be proclaimed future empress of the galaxy. She explains the infant's feet were poisoned by brambles and amputated, replaced with metal prostheses. The delegation demands she bring Aghnar for inspection.

[Hall of Arms] Aghnar undergoes examination by three priestesses. Found in alpha-mode with no killer programming, he is permitted to proceed. In a circular chamber he is coerced into a humiliating inspection of his claimed dual sex organs; he responds by deploying bladed mechanical components from his prosthetic lower legs and attacking.

[Combat and psychic battle] Aghnar realizes the priestess-assassins float because their prostheses are infused with epyphite. He exploits their weightlessness and kills multiple airborne attackers. A Shabda-Oud attacker then invokes the mental power of the Shabda-Oud against Honorata; she merges with an older silver-haired figure in the 'mind's shadow,' absorbs his energy, and unleashes a decisive counterblast. Aghnar achieves a major victory but is left exhausted.

[Cetacyborg battle] Othon engages the Cetacyborg, a colossal living bio-mechanical vessel too heavily armored for direct assault. He allows himself to be swallowed, pilots his metacraft through the corrosive interior, locates the servo-brain, and fires all his weapons simultaneously, destroying the creature in a supernova-scale explosion.

[Return and retreat decision] Othon returns to his maxi-protonic tower gravely ill: cetacyborg intestinal acids have corroded his lungs. He warns that the entire Shabda-Oud clan is approaching. He instructs Aghnar in warrior philosophy—adapt like water, renounce attachment to glory—and declares the Metabaron clan will go underground and re-emerge in years. The Metabunker is loaded with a metacraft and cargo trunks in preparation for departure.

[Honorata's revelation and sacrifice] At the embarkation, Honorata reveals she cannot leave: a micro-bomb inseparable from her artificial heart was implanted by her Shabda-Oud superiors. Removing it would kill her; she stays so the others can escape. Seven Cetycoborgs are detected by ultra-radar. Othon and Aghnar board the Metabunker and depart.

[Death and vow] Honorata's heart-bomb detonates. Othon forces Aghnar to witness the explosion, imprinting the memory as a foundation for a blood vow to destroy the Shabda-Oud. The Metabunker escapes into deep space. Tonto recounts the events to Lothar and mourns Honorata; another robot forcibly removes Tonto's verbal-memory plate and ersatz-emotion plug. The episode ends with the caption: 'The Trials of Aghnar.'
locations: Okhar (planet with carnivorous flowers and orbital defenses; primary site of the Shabda-Oud confrontation and Honorata's death)
The Castaka fortress / maxi-protonic tower (Othon's residence; ground-level setting for initiation, interrogation, and departure scenes)
Sacred mountain of Ansirma (exile training site where Honorata raised Aghnar)
The Metabunker (mobile war machine and escape vehicle; contains a metacraft, cargo, and an acid lake in its lower interior)
Hall of Arms (examination chamber with three priestesses; site of Aghnar's assessment and subsequent combat)
Interior of the Cetacyborg (organic-mechanical body with corrosive acids, intestinal passages, and a servo-brain control node)
Space approach to Okhar (route of Mother Superior's cautious Shabda-Oud vessel)
Industrial complex with suspended structure (frame-story location where Lothar's robot servant waits)
lore_laws: Epyphite is an anti-gravity substance; contact during birth makes a person permanently lighter than air; steel weights at waist and ankles counteract this effect; epyphite can also be infused into prostheses to make them airborne in combat
A person can be impregnated using a drop of a warrior's blood as a substitute for conventional conception
Metabaron initiation canonically includes ritual bodily mutilation and prosthetic replacement, a custom originating with Aghnar's ordeal
A chronomatrix can determine the precise age at which a person's scar tissue formed
Psycho-touch (psychic scanning) detects hidden surveillance; examiners also physically search for concealed weapons; alpha-mode is a recognized brain state indicating absence of killer programming
A catayborg controller can be rendered inactive for approximately two hours using a substance called pentalina
A bio-electrogram exists and can be accidentally or deliberately activated, with unpredictable consequences
The Cetacyborg's exterior skin resists heavy weapons; its sole critical vulnerability is the internal servo-brain, reachable only by infiltration through the body
Cetacyborg intestinal acids are corrosive enough to severely damage a person's lungs
An artificial heart can be converted into an unremovable bomb; extracting the device kills the host
The Shabda-Oud enforces loyalty by implanting lethal devices in operatives; betrayal triggers automatic death
The 'mind's shadow' is a psychic space where two individuals can merge and share energy, immediately amplifying offensive capability
Reprogramming is a punishment for robotic beings; internal components including verbal-memory plates and ersatz-emotion plugs are physically removable
A Harana-class robo-transporter is described as an organic vessel capable, if its sedated catayborg reactivates under hostile conditions, of reducing a planet to rubble
The Shabda-Oud sought a hermaphrodite child to proclaim as a perfect androgyne and future empress of the galaxy, using that child as a political instrument to seize the imperial throne
major_events: Metabunker split in half by the Master's energy beam; emergency reactor activation reunites the halves above an acid lake (pp. 03-05)
Robots forensically challenge the current Metabaron's invincibility using a chronomatrix to date an eyebrow scar; scar origin deferred to a future episode (pp. 06-07)
Shabda-Oud delegation interrogates Honorata under psychic sweep about the promised hermaphrodite child, now age seven, who was never delivered (p. 12)
Aghnar passes Hall of Arms examination and ambushes priestess-assassins using blade-prostheses, defeating multiple airborne attackers by exploiting their epyphite-infused prostheses (pp. 14-16)
Psychic battle: Honorata merges with an older figure in the mind's shadow and defeats a Shabda-Oud psychic attacker (p. 17)
Othon destroys the Cetacyborg from within: intentionally swallowed, navigates with metacraft to servo-brain, fires all weapons simultaneously (pp. 19-23)
Othon returns to maxi-protonic tower with acid-corroded lungs; announces Metabaron clan will hide in Metabunker (p. 24)
Honorata reveals her artificial heart is an unremovable Shabda-Oud bomb; she voluntarily stays behind as Othon and Aghnar flee (pp. 26-27)
Honorata's heart-bomb detonates; Othon indoctrinates Aghnar with the memory and vows Shabda-Oud annihilation (pp. 28-29)
Metabunker escapes into infinite space; Tonto's emotion plug and verbal-memory plate are forcibly removed; 'The Trials of Aghnar' announced (p. 30)
open_uncertainties: The origin of the Metabaron's right-eyebrow scar is explicitly deferred to a future episode; the scar's cause is unresolved within this volume
The identity of the older silver-haired figure who offers energy to Honorata in the mind's shadow is not stated on any page
The exact identity and physical nature of the primary saga narrator (large armored or cybernetic face/screen presence) are not fully established
Whether all the floating prosthetic attackers in the Hall of Arms battle belong to Aghnar or are a separate group equipped with similar epyphite-infused prostheses is ambiguous
The exact relationship between Honorata and the gray-haired muscular man who stage-manages the Shabda-Oud reception ceremony is not clarified
The blue spherical element seen during the robots' chronomatrix analysis of the Metabaron's eyebrow scar is unidentified
The identity and function of 'Big One,' used to display and enlarge the Metabaron's image during the forensic debate, are unclear
Whether the Shabda-Oud's demanded child was always Aghnar (male) or whether a true hermaphrodite was separately conceived and lost is not resolved
The precise nature of the large egg-shaped object called the 'sacred Shabda-Oud craft' displayed during the lady-ambassadors' ceremony is unexplained
The cover's armored figure holding the ornate engraved firearm is never identified in the story pages
recurring_motifs: Prosthetic body parts as simultaneous initiation rite, disability, and weapon
Epyphite (anti-gravity substance) recurring across birth, childhood grounding, combat exploitation, and prosthetic infusion
Ritual enforced witnessing: Aghnar is made to watch and endure rather than be protected
Self-sacrifice as the supreme expression of love within the Metabaron family lineage
The Tonto-Lothar narrative frame: saga recounted with comic interruptions, deliberate deferrals, and emotional asides
The Shabda-Oud as institutional body-control antagonist: hermaphrodite mandates, bomb-hearts, psychic weaponry
Concealing a fatal truth until revelation can no longer prevent the event it describes
Parent imprinting child with a parent's death as the moral origin of an inherited vendetta
title: The Snare of Okhar
